crop.notes: Two consecutive items under THE CITY: the Mace challenge story and a short follow-up 'Allen Returned. No Truth in the Report of a Fight.' Both about Allen.

ocr.notes: Several errors: image has '$5,000 aside' and '$2,500 aside' where OCR has pounds; 'will give him a grand benefit'; 'back up their opinions with big money'; final item 'it may be accepted' not 'realized'. Place printed 'Neenerville' (Kennerville).

title.suggested: Prospects of a fight between Tom Allen and Jem Mace

summary.suggested: The St. Louis Evening Dispatch reported that Jem Mace challenged Tom Allen from London and that Allen accepted, but a later item the same day said Allen, back from Chicago, called the report of a match a fraud.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'St. Louis Dispatch', Saturday Evening, November 20, 1875; named per rubric rule for pre-1878 Dispatch.

facts.fact: After the failed Rooke match, Allen issued a challenge to fight any man in or out of the country for $2,500 to $5,000 a side and the championship of the world, catch weights, London rules
A letter signed by Jem Mace, dated London Oct. 27, challenged Allen to fight within fifty miles of Detroit or Pittsburgh for £200 or £1,000 a side, saying Mace would sail from London Dec. 5
Mace's letter stated he beat Allen at Kennerville (printed 'Neenerville'), Louisiana, in May 1870, in ten rounds and forty-four minutes, for $2,500 a side and the title
Allen went to Chicago and was reported to have met Harry Hill and Barney Aaron and signed articles for a $5,000-a-side fight with Mace
Allen returned from Chicago and said there was no truth in the report that he had put up a forfeit for a fight with Mace, calling the whole thing a fraud

notes: The paper contradicts itself: the main story reports the Mace challenge and signed articles, the follow-up says Allen denied it and Mace was in Leeds in the poultry business.
